findings.file: StepType.java (UNKNOWN comment) + StepTypeReadConverter.java javadoc + audit-fix/report.json self_review
findings.issue: Documentation-accuracy nit (not a code defect): the comments/report assert UNKNOWN is rejected at the 'Jackson DTO boundary (@NotNull StepType) with a 400 before persistence'. That is imprecise — UNKNOWN is now a VALID enum constant, so a client literally POSTing stepType:"UNKNOWN" deserializes fine through Jackson and PASSES @NotNull; it is actually FunnelService.validateSteps (case UNKNOWN -> throw invalidStep) that rejects it, as a 422, not a 400. The end guarantee (UNKNOWN can never be saved as a valid step) HOLDS and is sound — validateSteps runs on every create(204)/update(309)/activate(309)/test-run(384) path — but the stated mechanism (Jackson 400) is wrong; the real gate is the validateSteps 422. Worth correcting the comment for future maintainers so nobody removes the validateSteps UNKNOWN case believing Jackson already blocks it.
findings.recommendation: Adjust the StepType.java / StepTypeReadConverter.java wording to credit FunnelService.validateSteps (422) as the author-input gate, not Jackson/@NotNull. The validateSteps UNKNOWN case is load-bearing — keep it.

findings.dimension: Architecture (1) — inherent property of tolerant-read, not a regression
findings.issue: The read converter applies to ALL StepType reads, including the funnels (definition) collection — not only funnel_executions. duplicate() copies an originally-persisted funnel's steps via copyOf and saves the copy WITHOUT calling validateSteps (line 282). So a hypothetical LEGACY funnel DEFINITION carrying a removed stepType (surviving the Decision-4 wipe) would read back as an UNKNOWN step and could be duplicated into a NEW draft containing a real UNKNOWN step. This is benign and NOT a defect introduced by the fix: (a) the copy is a draft; (b) activation re-runs validateSteps (line 309) which throws 422 on UNKNOWN, so it can never go active; (c) only active funnels enroll/execute, and the engine terminal-fails UNKNOWN anyway. The precondition is exactly the legacy-survivor population MAJ-1 exists to tolerate, and 'tolerate, never crash' is the intended posture. Flagging only for completeness — no action needed unless a future phase lets drafts execute.
findings.recommendation: None (acceptable residual). If duplicate() ever needs to surface a corrupt source, a validateSteps call there would catch it — but it is not required for safety today.
